Release scope and compatibility

Source: vignettes/release-scope.Rmd
release-scope.Rmd

ldfreq 0.4.0 is a fixed stable GitHub distribution for tracing lexical descriptions from original texts and counting conditions to research tables and reports. It is not a CRAN release. Install the named archive or fixed tag in the installation instructions; keep that archive, original inputs and complete saved results for later reuse.

Development 0.4.0.9001 adds a separately sourced occurrence-MCA example, absent from stable 0.4.0. It uses the existing optional ca package, with complete indicator rows, equal occurrence weights, unadjusted inertia and original source links. Category coding and inference remain the researcher’s responsibility. It adds no exported API, required dependency, core calculation or bundled resource. The stable-release tables below continue to describe the fixed 0.4.0 archive.

Development 0.4.0.9002 lets that MCA plot use separately named display labels for long occurrence IDs. The original IDs, saved fits and numerical results are unchanged; save the display mapping with the complete analysis record.

Development 0.4.0.9003 adds a separately sourced textbook progression example. It joins saved concordance matches to ordered pages, Units and selected sections, retaining missing material and the scope available after a declared teaching introduction. It is a descriptive example, not an automatic learning-effect assessment.

Development 0.4.0.9004 adds a separately sourced DDL preparation example. It writes selected, reviewed phrase occurrences and teacher-written prompts to learner HTML, a separate teacher CSV and a complete private record. Original sources and pending decisions remain intact; it does not conduct or evaluate a classroom lesson.

Development 0.4.0.9006 adds eight public entry points for research tables, concordance/dispersion, collocations and keyness. These interfaces preserve the previous counting and missingness rules; they do not broaden the statistical claims or add an analyzer. A new concordance class supports plot(). Original sourced names and plain-list records remain supported. The updated specialist guides use these public calls; install the 9006 archive to follow them.

What is stable, experimental or an example?

Stable means the documented computational and compatibility contract is maintained. It does not mean that a measure is valid for every population, text length, language or research claim. Method, schema, preprocessing and resource contract versions are separate from the package version.

Surface Status in 0.4.0 Boundary
Eleven default lexical-diversity metrics; explicit Maas/MTLD variants; local MATTR; specifications, plans, batches, tables and plots Stable computational contracts Ordered tokens and explicit parameters determine the result. Short-input failures remain NA with reasons; advisory length guidance is not a precision guarantee.
English/Unicode tokenization, supplied lemma/POS/flemma annotations, exact overlap and reference coverage Stable documented contracts English rules are explicit options. Unicode tokenization is not a Japanese morphological analyzer. Supplied labels and dictionaries require their own justification.
NJ8 levels, TUBELEX frequency, supplied lexical norms, adjacent n-gram frequencies/comparisons and paired scored responses Stable documented contracts Preserve the declared resource, units, denominator and coverage. Neither high coverage nor frequency establishes vocabulary knowledge or proficiency. The n-gram reference builder remains experimental.
Bundled NJ8, TUBELEX, MorphoLex and BNC/COCA resources; MorphyNet reader/example excerpt Fixed attributed resource versions The release does not change the resource bytes or rights. MorphoLex includes noncommercial restrictions. Consult the installed notices and resource manifest before redistribution. A fixed resource does not make every downstream analysis stable.
Expected-TTR D Experimental estimator, explicit opt-in Excluded from default metrics and presets. It fits an exact expectation curve; it is not CLAN VOCD, and CLAN equivalence is not established.
Family profiles; annotation import/alignment/evaluation; MASC/quanteda adapters; n-gram reference builder; ambiguity and contextual-model review/evaluation/baselines; adjective–noun dependencies Experimental interfaces Existing help and interface versions continue to apply. Models and human decisions remain distinct. Alignment and replay checks do not establish analyzer or model accuracy.
Study tables, corpus search/dispersion, collocation, keyness, readability, traced syntax and CA/classical MDS Documented, explicitly sourced examples Installed helpers are not exported APIs. Pin the package archive and preserve complete records. Examples connect existing calculations to source occurrences and reporting; they do not automatically choose a model or justify an inferential claim.

Stable 0.4.0 has 57 exports; development 0.4.0.9006 has 65. The eight new entry points have a documented initial interface; their formulas and analysis scope are those of the earlier examples. Stable release status does not remove the experimental labels in help or change the stability column returned by lexdiv_methods(). An example helper is located with system.file() and loaded with sys.source() as its guide shows; it has no separate ?function help entry. See ?ldfreq for the input and guide map.

Languages and external tools

Route Verified scope and requirements Limits
English core and profiles Authored counts, numerical reference fixtures, input/batch/missingness checks and saved-record replay; required packages are digest and stringi. A tokenizer/lexical unit must suit the research question. NJ8 and bundled TUBELEX target English; generic tokens do not establish Treebank alignment.
Japanese Complete caller-supplied, source-aligned annotations; the guide names the optional gibasa/MeCab, dictionary and external Sudachi routes used in comparisons. Specific pinned analyses support those examples. The package does not bundle a general Japanese parser, promise agreement between all dictionaries, or implement a Japanese readability score.
English readability Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level with visible sentence, word and syllable counts; an optional nsyllable route distinguishes dictionary matches and fallback estimates. Unresolved pronunciation and exclusions stay explicit. Agreement with the formulas does not validate comprehension or grade placement in a new population.
English syntactic complexity MLC, MLT and DC/C from traced original L2SCA outputs, with pinned Stanford tools/models, trees, query matches and original text. The authored offline example requires no parser. The external runner requires the documented local Python/Java tools and separately acquired software/models. It is not a generic parser adapter or a parser-accuracy validation.
CA and classical MDS CA uses optional ca; classical MDS uses stats::cmdscale() with Jaccard presence/absence or Hellinger distances. Records preserve exclusions, feature selection, eigenvalues and source links. Dense-matrix limits apply. Negative eigenvalues and reconstruction are reported, without automatic correction. Configurations are descriptive, not ability scales or group-effect tests.
Repeated observations and model tables Explicit planned observations, submitted documents and result specifications; an optional lme4 example uses an ordinary selected table. No automatic missing-data mechanism, outcome selection, model choice or causal interpretation is supplied.
MASC and other corpora Mini-MASC 1.0 Penn annotations and supported modern MASC 3.0.0 document-header layouts. Only 122 of 392 documents in the audited MASC 3.0.0 archive met the reader rules. Whole-corpus MASC/OANC support is not claimed; corpus access and rights remain separate.

The package declares R >= 4.1.0. Release checks cover the named source archive on current R for Linux, macOS and Windows, R-devel on Linux, and the R 4.1 minimum on Linux. Ordinary checks also exercise a genuine C locale and resource reconstruction. C-locale checks do not cover every Unicode-dependent path: tests requiring UTF-8 paths are explicitly skipped. The fixed release’s evidence records give the actual R, OS and dependency versions; these are tested configurations, not a promise about every older OS or future dependency release.

The R 4.1 diagnostic omits optional gibasa and textstem, whose current versions require newer R, and uses compatible Matrix, MASS and readxl versions. Use a current R installation for their optional routes. Python, Java, MeCab, external dictionaries and trained models are not required for the core R calculations. Their specific guide checks are separate from the R/OS matrix; the matrix does not execute every externally supplied model or corpus.

MCA, nonmetric MDS, Japanese readability, a universal ability scale and a new model-fitting API are not included. Their absence does not leave an unfinished step in the documented CA/classical-MDS or reporting workflows.

Moving from an earlier version

From 0.3.0.9019: calculations, exports, schemas, helpers and resources are unchanged. New calculations record package version 0.4.0. Reopening an older RDS must preserve its original calculation version and session information; do not replace those fields with the currently installed version.

From 0.1.0 or 0.2.0: the intervening changes below affect interpretation or compatibility. Retain the old archive and results before computing again.

  1. Core contract 0.2.0 uses no-minimum MTLD, with method ID mtld_seq_bidir_dirmean_lt_nomin_linear_tail_v1. The former min10 method remains explicitly available in lexdiv_variant_metrics(). Do not mix their values under one unlabeled MTLD column. See the migration section of ?lexdiv_metrics and the formula-variant help.
  2. Default metric results have eleven rows. Canonical and length-comparison presets contain eleven and thirteen requests. lexdiv_metric_ids() still lists twelve supported metrics, including experimental expected-TTR D. Select that estimator explicitly when it is part of the study design.
  3. Recreate old specifications and plans with current lexdiv_spec() and lexdiv_plan() before new calculations. Specification hashes include the core contract version, even for an unchanged formula. Read saved results without editing their IDs or values; comparison and plot checks reject unlike measurement identities.
  4. Preprocessing contract 0.1.0 objects must be recreated from original text and explicit annotations. The current 0.4.0 contract retains valid 0.3.0 objects and 0.2.0 Unicode objects. A legacy object without recorded textstem dictionary identity cannot establish strict lemma comparability. Do not manually fill provenance fields to bypass validation.
  5. TUBELEX contract 0.2.0 rejects known tokenizer mismatch by default. Prepare compatible terms, or explicitly record a sensitivity analysis with tokenization_mismatch = "allow". Character-vector alignment remains unverified. NJ8 contract 0.2.0 defaults to the bundled list when wordlist is omitted or NULL; explicit external lists retain their own identity.
  6. Version 0.2.0 corrected cancellation in near-saturated expected-TTR D without changing its estimator or method ID. Keep the package version as well as the method ID when comparing historical calculations. Details and the numerical correction are recorded in NEWS.

Pre-1.0 breaking changes require a minor-version increment and an explicit migration explanation. Exported functions, arguments, methods and schemas require a documented deprecation cycle before removal. The package-level lifecycle policy also separates formula, preprocessing and resource changes from cosmetic fixes.

Saving, citing and interpreting a result

Save original text, complete result objects, study metadata, selections and review decisions together. Keep external resource/model/dictionary identities and the calculation-session record. CSV display tables alone cannot recover source spans, missingness or full provenance. The guides include persistent RDS saving and separate-session reopening without rerunning external models.

citation("ldfreq") derives the package version from the installed copy. Report the version actually used for calculation, method IDs, parameters, word unit, preprocessing and resource versions. Cite the relevant methods and resources as well as the software. A later reporting session does not change the identity of the stored measurements. Calculation versions shown in saved example output identify the original run; they are not replaced by the version used to reopen or report that record.

The release evidence distinguishes successful computation/replay, agreement with independent numerical or software references, and empirical measurement validity. The first two do not prove the third. The documentation checks use independent development sessions; they are not a usability study with novice researchers. Population-level claims still need an appropriate research design.
